Global Industrial Machinery Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Industrial Machinery Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. Please allow a moment for our system to process the request. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Industrial Machinery Inc.'s results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Emily Carter, Chief Executive Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; and Kevin Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Emily Carter.

Emily Carter (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Global Industrial Machinery Inc.'s performance for Q2 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We delivered strong revenue performance across geographic regions, with North America leading the way amid reshoring trends. Our aftermarket parts and services saw impressive growth, now contributing over half of total revenue and providing high-margin stability. Automation and digital offerings accelerated sharply, driving efficiency gains for both us and our customers. Operating margins expanded notably by segment, showcasing our diversified portfolio's resilience. Price-cost dynamics played out favorably, with disciplined pricing more than offsetting raw material inflation. We're optimistic on end-market growth in the near and medium term, fueled by secular tailwinds in semis, aero, and electrification. And we're raising our operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, reflecting productivity gains and strategic execution.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Robert Hayes to provide more detail on our financial results.

Robert Hayes (CFO):
Thank you, Emily. Turning to our financial performance, Global Industrial Machinery Inc. reported $2.8 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 12% increase year-over-year on an organic basis. Gross margin was 32.8%, driven by favorable product mix, supply chain efficiencies, and pricing realization. Operating expenses were $490 million, resulting in an operating income of $420 million. Our net income for the quarter was $320 million, or $1.85 per share.

Good morning again, everyone. Before I go further, let me provide some color on our operating margin performance this quarter and our forward guidance, as this has been a focal point. Q2 delivered a segment-adjusted operating margin of 15.2%, up 120 basis points year-over-year and 40 basis points above the high end of our prior guide. This was powered by heavy content wins in automation systems for EV battery plants and disciplined pricing, where we captured an average 4.2% realization across core OEM equipment lines like CNC machining centers and hydraulic systems. Gross margin expansion benefited from our just-in-time inventory model with suppliers like Nucor and Alcoa, reducing working capital days to 68 from 75 last year.

We faced offsets from wage pressures up 5.8% in U.S. and European factories and a 12% spike in alloy surcharges tied to LME copper prices. But proactive hedging covering 70% of FY24 exposure and our Enterprise Lean Sigma program across 15 plants kept OpEx leverage at 17.6% of sales.

For Q3, we're guiding segment-adjusted operating margin to 14.5% to 15.5%. The midpoint implies a 20 basis point sequential decline from Q2, due to seasonally softer volumes in construction equipment like skid steers and wheel loaders during the summer non-residential slowdown. We're assuming flat-to-down 2% organic revenue growth quarter-over-quarter, with steady demand in mining and oil & gas but softening in ag equipment post-harvest.

Key positives include pricing and mix providing a 150 basis point tailwind from full realization of 4-6% hikes on fluid power products like Parker-compatible hydraulic pumps, plus richer mix from aftermarket parts up 18% YoY at 45%+ margins. Aftermarket now at 28% of total revenue, up from 24% two years ago, driven by predictive maintenance via our GIM Connect IoT platform, much like Honeywell and Siemens in controls.

Volumes and regions are neutral to -50 bps: North America shines with 5-7% growth in material handling for data centers from IIJA tailwinds; Europe flat on high energy costs crimping gas turbine components; Asia mixed with strong semi capex in Taiwan but China property drag.

Cost headwinds of -100 bps from steel at $750/ton above our $650 hedge and Rust Belt labor tightness are countered by FANUC robotic lines in Ohio cutting direct labor 15% on weldments, similar to Caterpillar's autonomy efforts.

For the full year, we're raising FY24 operating margin guide to 15.0% to 15.5% from 14.5-15.0%, assuming 6-8% organic growth FX neutral and $120 million in productivity from digital transformation like AI-optimized supply chain via SAP S/4HANA and digital twins for compressors, akin to GE's Predix. Localization at 85% North American content dodges tariffs.

Margins set to inflect to 16-17% in FY25 as we scale electrified drivetrains via our e-axle JV with Dana, like Deere's autonomy pivot. ESG premiums on low-emission CNC mills add 50 bps for Tesla and Boeing suppliers. With peers like Ingersoll Rand and Allegion at similar multiples but less automation exposure, risks like ISM PMI below 48 or Red Sea disruptions are offset by our $1.2 billion cash and 2.1x net debt-to-EBITDA.

Now, diving deeper into operating margin by segment for the quarter, which reflects our portfolio's resilience. Overall group margins expanded 130 basis points to 12.5%, our best Q3 since 2019, beating 11.5-12.0% guidance via automation mix, cost controls, and 88% factory utilization up from 82%.

Our segments: Industrial Automation at 32% revenue, Heavy Machinery 28%, Precision Components 22%, Energy Equipment 18%.

Industrial Automation margins hit 18.5%, up 170 bps on $1.2 billion revenue up 12%, with software/services at 42% mix. Book-to-bill 1.25x, $2.8 billion backlog up 15%. Pricing offset semi costs; Factory 4.0 like Rockwell's FactoryTalk boosted throughput 11% in Greenville and Monterrey. North America 22% margins on CHIPS/IRA reshoring; EMEA 16% eased by Dortmund solar; APAC 19% on EV cobots outselling Fanuc.

Heavy Machinery at 10.2%, down 130 bps on flat $1.05 billion amid capex pinch, but adjusted 11% sans writedown. Utilization 85%; telematics mix lifted ASP 3%, services 28% at 25%+ margins. North America 12% on IIJA backlog; EMEA 8% on Euro slowdowns; APAC 11% on iron ore.

Precision Components 14.8%, up 250 bps on 9% growth to $820 million, asset-light with 92% utilization. Additive manufacturing cut lead times 30% for GE/Boeing; North America 17% on F-35; APAC 13% on TSMC.

Energy Equipment 8.7%, up 90 bps on 7% to $680 million, LNG offsetting oil softness. CCUS/wind pivot; North America 10% on Exxon; Middle East 9%; Europe 6%. HyCore electrolyzer targets 12% by 2025.

Aggregate high-margin cyclical split, gross at 32.5% despite 4% inflation via 65% localization and RPA procurement. Q4 guide 12.8-13.3%; $4.2 billion backlog, 45% FCF conversion.

On price-cost dynamics impacting margins, inputs at 55% COGS faced steel up 12% to $850/ton HRC, aluminum 8% to $2,450, copper $9,200 on disruptions and demand. North America 15% steel from IIJA, Europe 18% on gas, APAC 10%.

Mitigated by 60% steel hedging saving $45 million, 20% aluminum shift to UAE/Indonesia, Value Engineering 2.0 subbing AHSS cutting intensity 8%.

Pricing averaged 6.5%, 7-9% on AX-5000 presses for 8.2% ASP lift; aftermarket 5-7% on consumables via ApexCare IoT. Gross to 33.2% Q4, 31.8% full-year, EBITDA 22.4%; Precision 35.5%, Construction 29.8%.

2024 normalizes with steel deflation 5-7%, 4-6% pricing on electric forklifts at 38% margins.

Aftermarket generated $1.45 billion, 52% total revenue up from 48%, 18% growth constant currency 20%. Parts $900 million up 16%, services $550 million up 22% on lifecycle contracts like Cat Rebuild. Margins 48% via sourcing and IntelliParts.

Americas 21% on mining; EMEA 15% on wind; APAC 14% on infra. GIE Connect IoT on 65% base cuts downtime 28%, digital twins 40% faster service. FY growth 16-18% to 53-54% mix.

Revenue by region totaled $2.8 billion up 12% organic. North America $538 million 42% up 18% on semis/CHIPS, Monterrey expansion. Europe $358 million 28% up 8% on aero/renewables despite energy. APAC $307 million 24% up 15% on semis/EV. Rest $77 million 6% up 22% on LatAm/ME.

Q4 11-13% organic. Backlog $4.5 billion.

On end-market outlook, near-term FY25 4-6% organic moderating from 8%, semis 12-15% on AI fabs, aero 5-7%, auto/EV 2-4%, energy mixed. NA 6-8%, Europe 1-3%, APAC 4-6%.

Medium FY26-28 7-9% CAGR on automation 10-12%, electrification 8-10%, reshoring. $1.2 billion CapEx, Zero-Waste program.

Automation/digital $285 million up 28%, recurring $112 million 39%, margins 48.2%. AutoForge orders 35%, IndusNet 52% with 150k sensors cutting downtime 25-30%. Bundling boosts win rates 15%, service costs down 28%. NA 45%, Europe 30%, APAC 55%. FY $1.15-1.2 billion.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and generating consistent cash flow. Now, I will hand over to Maria Gonzalez, COO, for an operational update.

Maria Gonzalez (COO):
Thank you, Robert. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing customer service across our global footprint. We've leveraged data analytics from our IoT platforms to pinpoint improvements, driving utilization to 88% and reducing scrap by 14% through lean programs. Investments in employee training have built a skilled workforce ready for automation ramps, with cross-training in AI tools and safety protocols. We've localized 65% of sourcing to counter disruptions, and our reman centers are scaling to support aftermarket surge.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Kevin Patel, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Kevin Patel (CTO):
Thank you, Maria. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We're investing heavily in R&D—8% of sales this year—in AI, machine learning, IoT, edge computing, and 5G for Industry 4.0. Our solutions improve predictive maintenance, like IndusNet's anomaly detection slashing downtime 30%, and optimize operations with digital twins simulating what-ifs 50x faster. Our new IntelliBot Gen3 cobots are exceeding expectations, with 35% order growth and 20-25% CapEx ROI for customers in under 18 months, boosting our OEE from 75% to 90% in deployments. We've deployed quantum-secure AI and generative models for prescriptive optimization, positioning us ahead in semis fabs and EV lines.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Jennifer Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Kevin Patel:
Thanks, Jennifer. Automation spending remains robust, with our segment up 28% in Q2 as labor shortages and reshoring drive demand. We're seeing 35% growth in robotic welding cells like AutoForge, integrating AI vision for 40% scrap reduction, and IndusNet IoT growing 52%, connecting 150,000 sensors for 25-30% downtime cuts. North America leads on EV/CHIPS, Europe on Green Deal efficiency, APAC on semis. Book-to-bill 1.25x, backlog up, guiding 25-30% FY growth as peers like Rockwell scale similarly. Secular 10-12% CAGR ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Kim (Goldman Sachs):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Robert Hayes:
Great question, David. Price-cost netted positive this quarter despite steel up 12%, aluminum 8%, copper spikes. Hedged 60-70% exposure saving $45 million, diversified sourcing, value engineering cut material 8% with AHSS. Pricing 6.5% average, full pass-through on aftermarket consumables. Gross expanded 250 bps YoY to 33.2%, with 2024 deflation tailwinds and 4-6% hikes planned. Localization and RPA keep leverage intact.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel (JPMorgan):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

Emily Carter:
Absolutely, Sarah. Sustainability is core, with ESG premiums adding 50 bps already. Our Zero-Waste Machining cuts coolant 40% via MQL, Dortmund 50 MW solar targets 15% scope 2 reduction, 30% recycled content goal. Electrified drivetrains, HyCore electrolyzers for CCUS/wind, low-emission CNC for Tesla/Boeing align with mandates. REPowerEU, IRA incentives boost renewables exposure up 30%, positioning for FY25 margin inflection.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Emily Carter (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Industrial Machinery Inc. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Thompson (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
